hints.title: Absolute Value Simplification
hints.text: Notice that the pair condition simplifies to comparing absolute magnitudes: v[j] <= 2 * v[i].

hints.title: Ordered Search Window
hints.text: Sort the absolute values in ascending order to make the upper valid bound contiguous.

hints.title: Counting Valid Pairs
hints.text: For each index i, locate the furthest index j where v[j] does not exceed double v[i].

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def numberOfPairs(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        # A pair is perfect if |a - b| <= min(|a|, |b|)
        # For non-zero sorted absolute values: v[j] <= 2 * v[i]
        vals = sorted(abs(x) for x in nums)
        n = len(vals)
        ans = 0
        
        for i in range(n):
            target = 2 * vals[i]
            # Find rightmost index with value <= target
            idx = bisect.bisect_right(vals, target)
            ans += (idx - 1 - i)
            
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Sorting takes O(N log N), followed by binary search per element.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all pairs in a quadratic nested loop times out on large arrays.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Stores absolute values in a sorted vector of size N.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Simplify algebraic inequality to the ratio v[j] <= 2 * v[i] and sort.
